key_terms.definition: Drinking Water Treatment Plant; municipal facility treating raw surface/ground water to produce potable water.
Sant Joan Despí Drinking Water Treatment Plant near Barcelona, Spain, supplying ~40% of the metropolitan area's water.
Principal Component Analysis; unsupervised multivariate chemometric technique decomposing data into orthogonal scores and loadings to uncover dominant variance patterns.
Sum of squared residual errors measuring sample-to-model distance in PCA, identifying unusual outlying events and unmodeled disturbances.
Multivariate Statistical Process Control; statistical quality monitoring framework leveraging PCA scores and Q residuals for multi-sensor real-time event detection.
Total Organic Carbon (mg/L); sum of organic carbon species in raw water, associated with runoff and disinfection byproduct precursors.
Turbidity (UNF); measurement of light scattering by suspended particulate matter in river water.
UV absorbance at 254 nm (abs/100 cm); proxy for aromatic and humic organic matter fractions.
Electrical conductivity (μS/cm); proxy for dissolved ionic solutes and total mineralization.
Ammonium ion concentration (mg/L); indicator of untreated or poorly treated domestic wastewater discharge and agricultural runoff.
Two-year (2013-2014) hourly sensor time-series for 7 physicochemical parameters aligned via linear interpolation (16,333 measurements), used to reveal seasonal trends.
Six-month (July-November 2014) experimental dataset containing 346 strictly simultaneous 7-parameter readings, used for event detection and Q-residual fault diagnosis.
Weekly dataset spanning 52 days/weeks combining 14 variables (6 microbiological indicators, river flow, and 7 physicochemical parameters), used to evaluate microbial-physicochemical correlations.

# Document Overview: Chemometric Analysis for River Water Quality Assessment

## Core Thesis
Multivariate statistical analysis using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on continuous on-line sensor and laboratory data provides an effective chemometric tool to separate long-term seasonal cycles from short-term pollution events, identify organic, inorganic, and microbiological contamination episodes, and establish multivariate statistical process control thresholds at drinking water treatment plant intakes.

## Output Language
English

## Glossary of Key Terms and Acronyms
- **DWTP**: Drinking Water Treatment Plant (specifically the Sant Joan Despí plant, SJD DWTP, supplying Barcelona).
- **PCA**: Principal Component Analysis (unsupervised dimensionality reduction decomposing data matrices into score and loading matrices).
- **Q residuals**: Sum of squared residual errors quantifying deviations of individual samples from the PCA model subspace, used to detect abnormal contamination events.
- **MSPC**: Multivariate Statistical Process Control (real-time monitoring using PCA limits instead of isolated univariate parameter thresholds).
- **Parameters**: TURB (turbidity, UNF), TOC (total organic carbon, mg/L), UV254 (UV absorbance, abs/100 cm), COND (conductivity, μS/cm), NH4 (ammonium, mg/L), TEMP (temperature, °C), pH, Flow (m³/s).
- **Datasets**: Dataset 1 (two years of hourly sensor recordings, 16,333 aligned points), Dataset 2 (346 simultaneous sensor readings, July-Nov 2014), Dataset 3 (52 weekly observations combining 6 bacteriological indicators with 7 physicochemical parameters and flow).

## Section Overview
- **Abstract**: High-level overview of the study, data acquisition from sensors, 3-component PCA models, and the value of chemometrics for drinking water plant intake safety.
- **1. Introduction**: Mediterranean water scarcity context, SJD DWTP infrastructure (advanced ultrafiltration and reverse osmosis membranes), upstream stressors (potash salt mining, urban/industrial discharges), and limitations of univariate thresholding.
- **2. Material and methods**:
  - *2.1 Current water quality monitoring practices*: Traditional univariate threshold checking under ISO 22000.
  - *2.2 Data organization*: Architecture and features of Datasets 1, 2, and 3.
  - *2.3 Multivariate statistical analysis*: Mathematical formulation of PCA, singular value decomposition, scores, loadings, and Q residuals.
  - *2.4 Curve fitting of time series*: Fourier series harmonic decomposition modeling annual and semi-annual seasonal trajectories.
- **3. Results and discussion**:
  - *3.1 Seasonal variability (PCA Dataset 1)*: Separation of organic matter (PC1, 35%), inorganic/salinity (PC2, 24%), and pH (PC3, 13%), along with Fourier curve fits and meteorological validation.
  - *3.2 Event detection (PCA Dataset 2)*: Identification of three distinct short-term pollution episodes (extreme organic flush from rainfall, inorganic mining spill, and pH anomaly) via high Q residuals.
  - *3.3 Microbiological correlation (Dataset 3)*: Positive co-occurrence between bacterial contamination peaks (coliforms, enterococci, Clostridium) and organic runoff (TOC, UV254, TURB) during initial storm flushes.
  - *3.4 Practical recommendations*: Proposal for real-time PCA-based MSPC implementation at DWTP intakes using unified Q-residual thresholds.
- **4. Conclusions**: Summary of core findings, diagnostic fingerprinting of pollution sources, and operational value for early warning and water utility infrastructure protection.
